label: r4c3
name: flip, half batches, ent 0.01
hypothesis: Same as r3c1 but ent_coef 0.01. The higher entropy was added to stop an early collapse onto DONE, but with n_envs 128 the agent already learns quickly (0.29 training success at 25%). A lower entropy bonus should let the policy sharpen, so greedy and training behaviour match more closely and exact builds are more reliable. Refuted if dev success falls below about 0.92 or a seed collapses to DONE.
last_analysis: Rounds 1–3 found one big fix: actions are mirrored along x relative to the observation, and flipping the features before the footprint head fixes it (0 → 0.75). Every gain after that came from the recipe. Cutting ppo_epochs from 4 to 2 gave 0.93; 1 epoch gave 0.92. Halving n_envs to 128 so there are twice as many updates gave the best score, 0.949 (r3c1), and the fastest early learning (0.29 training success at 25% of training, against 0.00 before). Changes that did not help or made things worse: lr 2e-3 (0.933, within noise), gamma 0.99 (0.87), a deeper trunk (0.82), moving compute into the head (0.86) and a learned axis remap (0). Seed spread is about 2–5 points. The evidence says this budget is limited by how many updates training gets, not by the network's capacity. For this last round I keep r3c1's network and push the update-frequency lever further: smaller batches, 1 epoch with more samples, and lower entropy now that early learning is fast.
